transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it’s bridges. If I know I have to cross one and there’s no way around it, I start getting scared right away—before I’m even on it. My heart pounds, my hands get damp on the steering wheel or the armrest, and I get this terrible rush of fear.
Do you get this same rush of fear in other places where it might be hard to get away, like highways, tunnels, or crowded places?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it the same way in those other places. It’s mainly when it’s a bridge that I know I have to cross.
What is it about being on a bridge that scares you most?

I know it doesn’t make sense, really. I know cars go over those bridges all day long. But when I see a big high bridge coming up, or even on the map, it feels like it could just drop away underneath us. That’s what scares me most.
When you’re on a bridge, is the main fear that the bridge itself will collapse?

Yes, that’s really it. I know, in my head, that thousands of cars go over those bridges every day. But when I see a high one coming up, or even see it on the map, it just feels like the whole thing could drop away underneath us.
Do you avoid crossing bridges whenever you can?

Yes. For more than two years now, I’ve been planning errands and visits so I don’t have to cross bridges. I’ve stopped going to San Juan, and I don’t really do Seattle theater nights anymore because of it. If I absolutely have to cross one, I need to study the route ahead of time, go at the right time, and have someone with me. Even then I’m scared the whole way across.
Have you ever had one of these sudden rushes of fear when you were not around a bridge?
I don’t think so. I mean, I can’t recall that happening out of the blue. It’s usually tied to the bridge, or knowing I’m going to have to cross one.
When you think about crossing a bridge, is your fear mainly that the bridge will collapse?
Yes. I know it doesn’t make much sense, because so many cars cross them every day. But when I see a high bridge ahead, or even on the map, it feels like it could just give way underneath us.
